142	  schema_version: "2.0"
143	  description: >
144	    Ten-element hierarchical rubric for evaluating D4D YAML completeness and usability.
145	    Each element represents a complex metadata-driven goal and includes up to five measurable
146	    sub-elements. Scores can be computed at the element or sub-element level.
147	
148	  scoring_scale:
149	    element: 0–5
150	    sub_element: [0, 1]  # 0 = not present/fail, 1 = present/pass
151	
152	  rubric:
153	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
154	    - id: 1
155	      name: "Dataset Discovery and Identification"
156	      description: "Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?"
157	      sub_elements:
158	        - name: "Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)"
159	          field: ["doi", "rrid", "id"]
160	        - name: "Dataset Title and Description Completeness"
161	          field: ["title", "description"]
162	        - name: "Keywords or Tags for Searchability"
163	          field: ["keywords"]
164	        - name: "Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)"
165	          field: ["page", "resources"]
166	        - name: "Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)"
167	          field: ["parent_datasets", "related_datasets"]
168	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
169	
170	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
171	    - id: 2
172	      name: "Dataset Access and Retrieval"
173	      description: "Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?"
174	      sub_elements:
175	        - name: "Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined"
176	          field: ["license_and_use_terms", "ip_restrictions"]
177	        - name: "Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification"
178	          field: ["regulatory_restrictions", "confidentiality_level", "hipaa_compliant", "other_compliance", "governance_committee_contact"]
179	        - name: "Download URL or Platform Link Available"
180	          field: ["download_url"]
181	        - name: "Distribution Formats and File Types Specified"
182	          field: ["distribution_formats", "format", "media_type"]
183	        - name: "Related Datasets and External Resources Linked"
184	          field: ["related_datasets", "external_resources"]
185	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
186	
187	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
188	    - id: 3
189	      name: "Data Reuse and Interoperability"
190	      description: >
191	        Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?
192	
193	        Note: Evaluate whether the dataset is designed for integration with similar datasets,
194	        including: common identifiers for cross-dataset linking, standardized formats for data
195	        harmonization, and documented integration procedures.
196	      sub_elements:
197	        - name: "License Terms Allow Reuse"
198	          field: ["license_and_use_terms"]
199	        - name: "Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)"
200	          field: ["format", "encoding"]
201	        - name: "Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated"
202	          field: ["conforms_to", "conforms_to_schema"]
203	        - name: "Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined"
204	          field: ["variables"]
205	        - name: "Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)"
206	          field: ["intended_uses", "prohibited_uses", "discouraged_uses"]
207	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
208	
209	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
210	    - id: 4
211	      name: "Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards"
212	      description: "Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?"
213	      sub_elements:
214	        - name: "IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact"
215	          field: ["ethical_reviews", "human_subject_research", "data_protection_impacts"]
216	        - name: "Deidentification Method Described"
217	          field: ["is_deidentified"]
218	        - name: "Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment"
219	          field: ["participant_privacy", "reidentification_risk"]
220	        - name: "Informed Consent Obtained from Participants"
221	          field: ["informed_consent"]
222	        - name: "Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented"
223	          field: ["vulnerable_populations", "participant_compensation"]
224	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
225

230	      sub_elements:

233	        - name: "Number of Instances or Samples Reported"
234	          field: ["instances"]
235	        - name: "Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits"

238	          field: ["instances"]
239	        - name: "Data Quality, Anomalies, and Missing Data Documented"

241	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
242

244	    - id: 6
245	      name: "Data Provenance and Version Tracking"
246	      description: "Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?"
247	      sub_elements:
248	        - name: "Dataset Version Number Provided"
249	          field: ["version"]
250	        - name: "Version Access Methods Documented"
251	          field: ["version_access"]
252	        - name: "Change Descriptions and Errata Provided"
253	          field: ["errata", "updates"]
254	        - name: "Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated"
255	          field: ["updates"]
256	        - name: "Provenance, Source Derivation, and Raw Data Sources"
257	          field: ["was_derived_from", "release_notes", "raw_data_sources"]
258	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
259	
260	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
261	    - id: 7
262	      name: "Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency"
263	      description: "Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?"
264	      sub_elements:
265	        - name: "Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation"
266	          field: ["purposes"]
267	        - name: "Primary Research Objectives or Tasks"
268	          field: ["tasks"]

282	
283	        Note: Preprocessing and collection metadata may be represented as structured text
284	        descriptions OR as machine-readable provenance graphs (e.g., W3C PROV-O, workflow graphs).
285	        Evaluation should check for: (1) structured text descriptions OR (2) graph representations
286	        with entity-activity-agent relationships. Both formats are acceptable.
287	      sub_elements:
288	        - name: "Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described"

290	        - name: "Data Acquisition Methods Listed"
291	          field: ["acquisition_methods"]
292	        - name: "Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality"

294	        - name: "Software and Tools Documented"
295	          field: ["software_and_tools"]
296	        - name: "External Standards, Resources, and Imputation Protocols"
297	          field: ["external_resources", "conforms_to", "imputation_protocols"]
298	      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"
299	
300	    # ---------------------------------------------------- #
301	    - id: 9
302	      name: "Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure"
303	      description: "Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?"
304	      sub_elements:

306	          field: ["known_limitations"]
307	        - name: "Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)"

309	        - name: "Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted"

import json
import re as _re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

    from jsonschema import validate, ValidationError
except ImportError:
    print("ERROR: jsonschema package not installed")
    print("Install with: pip install jsonschema")
    sys.exit(1)


def load_schema(schema_path: Path) -> Dict:
    """Load JSON Schema file."""
    with open(schema_path, 'r') as f:
        return json.load(f)


def load_evaluation(eval_path: Path) -> Dict:
    """Load evaluation JSON file."""
    with open(eval_path, 'r') as f:
        return json.load(f)


#: Top-level keys of the shape that preceded the current agent contract.
#: rubric10 evaluations recorded before 2026 report `summary_scores` and
#: `element_scores`; the agents have instructed `overall_score` and `elements`
#: since. Such a record is not wrong, it is a different vintage — reporting it
#: as invalid buries the records that really are.
SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS = ("summary_scores", "element_scores")


def classify(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
    """Validate, distinguishing a superseded shape from a wrong value.

    Returns `("valid" | "superseded" | "invalid", errors)`.

    The distinction is the point. All 28 recorded evaluations failed before the
    schemas were brought up to the agents (#323), and "Invalid: 28" said nothing
    about which were merely old. Of the 20 that still fail, 12 predate the
    contract and 8 report `max_points: 84` — a maximum the rubric has never had
    (#314). Only the second kind is a defect in a record.
    """
    errors = []
    try:
        validate(instance=eval_data, schema=schema)
        return "valid", []
    except ValidationError as e:
        errors.append(f"Validation error: {e.message}")
        errors.append(f"  Path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.path)}")
        if e.schema_path:
            errors.append(f"  Schema path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.schema_path)}")
        if any(k in eval_data for k in SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS):
            return "superseded", errors
        return "invalid", errors

    """Back-compatible wrapper: superseded records are not valid."""
    status, errors = classify(eval_data, schema)

                     schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:

    Directory names and superseded shapes do not exempt a new output. This
    path reads only the files named by the caller, so an evaluator can check
    its own output without reading another evaluator's judgements (#833).
    """
    schema_dir = schema_dir or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src/download/prompts"

        try:
            doc = load_evaluation(path)

            if not valid:
                raise ValueError("\n".join(errors))
        except (OSError, ValueError, jsonschema.SchemaError) as exc:
            print(f"INVALID {path}: {exc}")
            failed = True
        else:
            print(f"VALID {path}: {declared}")
    return int(failed)


#: A directory whose name marks its contents as kept evidence rather than a
#: live artifact: an archive, a superseded set, or a dated snapshot of one
#: arm's scores. An invalid record in one of these is what an older
#: instrument produced and must not be rewritten to satisfy today's schema,
#: so it is reported and does not fail the run.
KEPT_DIR = _re.compile(r"^(?:_archive|superseded)|^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(?:[_-]|$)")

    """Is any directory between `base` and `path` an archive marker?"""
    return any(KEPT_DIR.match(part) for part in path.relative_to(base).parts[:-1])

    """Every evaluation JSON under `base`, at any depth.

    The loop was `{rubric}_semantic/concatenated/*.json` — one directory per
    rubric, one level deep (#833). That reached 28 of the 204 semantic
    artifacts on disk: not `label_aware/`, which is where every evaluation
    since 2026-08 lives and which the cross-arm table reads, not the dated
    per-arm subdirectories beside it, and not the archives. The rubric a file
    declares decides which schema it is judged against, so the directory does
    not have to.
    """
    return sorted(base.rglob("*_evaluation.json"))


def main(eval_base: Path | None = None, schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
    """Validate every evaluation JSON under `data/evaluation_llm`.

    The two roots are arguments so that the exit code — the thing #833 asked
    for, and the thing four tests of the helpers did not reach — can be
    exercised end to end over a tree built for the purpose.
    """
    base_dir = Path(__file__).parent.parent
    schema_dir = schema_dir or base_dir / "src" / "download" / "prompts"
    eval_base = eval_base or base_dir / "data" / "evaluation_llm"

    schemas = {
        "rubric10-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric10_semantic_schema.json"),
        "rubric20-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"),
    }

    eval_files = discover(eval_base)
    if not eval_files:
        print(f"No evaluation files found in {eval_base}")
        return 1

    print(f"Found {len(eval_files)} evaluation file(s) under {eval_base}\n")

    counts = {("live", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
    counts.update({("kept", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")})
    no_schema: Dict[str, int] = {}
    live_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []
    kept_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []

    for eval_file in eval_files:
        where = "kept" if is_kept(eval_file, eval_base) else "live"
        shown = eval_file.relative_to(eval_base)
        try:
            eval_data = load_evaluation(eval_file)
            if not isinstance(eval_data, dict):
                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"❌ {shown}: failed to load: {e}")
            counts[(where, "unreadable")] += 1
            continue

        rubric = eval_data.get("rubric", "unknown")
        if rubric not in schemas:
            # Named and counted, not skipped in silence: the presence-style
            # rubric10/rubric20 outputs have no schema in this repository, and
            # a reader of the summary should see that they were not judged.
            no_schema[str(rubric)] = no_schema.get(str(rubric), 0) + 1
            continue

        status, errors = classify(eval_data, schemas[rubric])
        counts[(where, status)] += 1
        if status == "invalid":
            (kept_invalid if where == "kept" else live_invalid).append((shown, errors))
        elif status == "superseded":
            print(f"🕐 {shown}: superseded shape — {errors[0]}")

    for label, rows in (("live", live_invalid), ("kept as evidence", kept_invalid)):
        for shown, errors in rows:
            print(f"❌ {shown} ({label}):")
            for error in errors:
                print(f"     {error}")

    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("SUMMARY (judged against a schema):")
    for where in ("live", "kept"):
        row = {k: counts[(where, k)] for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
        print(f"  {where:5}  valid {row['valid']:4}  superseded {row['superseded']:3}  "
              f"invalid {row['invalid']:3}  unreadable {row['unreadable']:3}")
    if no_schema:
        print("  no schema in this repository, not judged: "
              + ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in sorted(no_schema.items())))
    print("=" * 60)

    # A superseded record is historical output of a contract that no longer
    # applies, and one kept under an archive marker is evidence of what an
    # older instrument produced: reported, never rewritten to pass. Only a
    # live invalid artifact fails the run.
    return 0 if not live_invalid and not counts[("live", "unreadable")] else 1


def cli(argv: List[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--file", type=Path, action="append", dest="files",
                        help="validate this exact new output strictly; repeat for multiple files")
    parser.add_argument("--rubric", choices=("rubric10-semantic", "rubric20-semantic"),
                        help="require the named outputs to use this rubric")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.rubric and not args.files:
        parser.error("--rubric requires --file")
    return validate_outputs(args.files, args.rubric) if args.files else main()
